ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To break through Caizhou evokes the taking of a defended stronghold. In Chan records it becomes a compact victory-and-defeat verdict: a later word can complete the breakthrough, while a timely response can keep a position from being overrun.
EvidenceBody: Yunfeng says Nanquan’s final word saved him from having Caizhou broken; Dahui reverses the appraisal and says that very final word broke it at once. Muchen Daomin repeatedly applies the formula to cases and live hall turns. Langye Huijue says Guishan’s response kept the stronghold from being broken; two collections preserve that same Langye utterance, but it counts as one deployment class.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A named military capture is redeployed as an immediate appraisal of who held or lost the encounter.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The witnesses support a victory/defeat image, not a fixed claim that every use identifies the same doctrinal error; the near-loss forms and completed-breakthrough form deliberately point in opposite directions.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The witnesses reuse one capture image as a verdict; changed grammatical aspect does not create another referent.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The aliases expose capture, breakthrough, and near-defeat lookup routes visible in the corpus deployments.

ModifierControls.reason: 蔡州 is the fixed place-name in the capture formula; the sources vary completed breakthrough against narrowly avoided defeat, not grades or materials of a stronghold.

FamilyControls.reason: The retained witnesses include the core N泉/Zhaozhou appraisal and later independent hall redeployments rather than recension padding.
